d: Field of battle on the banks of the Idaspe. Curtains and overturned chariots, scattered soldiers, weapons, insignia and other leftovers of the army of Pore unleashed by Alexander. After the symphony is heard amazing weapons and military introments; in the alzar of the tent Soldiers fleeing. Pore, then Gandarte with bare swords.
Poro, then Timagen with a naked sword, followed by the Greeks, and Alexander.
Alexander, then Timagen with Erissena chained, two Indians and followed;
The fence of palms and cypresses with a pinion of the temple in the middle, dedicated to Bacchus in the palace of Cleofide. Cleofide with followers, at the end of Poro
Grand pavilion of Alexander near the Idaspe with view of the palace of Cleofide on the other side of the river. Alexander with Guards behind the pavilion and Timagen.

You can see several boats coming along the river, from which many Indians descend from the Cleofide Following bringing several gifts, and from the main landing the aforementioned Cleofide met by Alessandro. Cleofide and sayings.

A scattered campaign of ancient fabric with tents and military quarters prepared by Cleofide for the Greek army. Bridge over the Idaspe. Alessandro's large field arranged in order beyond the river, with elephants, towers, covered wagons and war machines. In the opening of the scene is heard symphony of military introments, in the time of which the bridge passes part of the Greek Soldiers and after them Alexander with Timagene, then Cleofide comes to meet him. Cleofide, Alessandro and Timagene, in Gandarte.
Poro exits from the left side of the scene without sword followed by Cleofide.
Alexander who goes out behind Poro's back holds him and disarms him, Greek soldiers and sayings.
Cleofide, Poro and Timagen with Guards.
Apartments in the palace of Cleofide. Cleofide and Gandarte.
Porticos of the royal gardens, Poro, then Erissena.
Erissena, then Alexander with two Guards.

Magnificent Temple dedicated to Bacchus with stake in the middle that then lights up. Alexander and Cleofide preceded by the choir of the Bacchanti who come out dancing. Guards, People and Ministers of the temple with faces. Indi Poro in side.
Timagen, then Gandarte, then Erissena and sayings.
